thread:
maya: Noticed a p95 bump on host-side after last kernel tuning. Mostly short streaming responses (<=64 tokens). Anyone else seeing host parse/stream work increase?
asher: Yep. I dug in with async profiler. Host parse + framing is ~55% of tail work now.
maya: can you paste the stack?
asher: paste:```
sampled-stack: request_entry -> parse_stream_frames -> incremental_utf8_check -> frame_flush -> grpc_write_small -> syscall
hot: frame_flush (38%), incremental_utf8_check (22%), grpc_write_small (18%)
```
devon: interesting. frame_flush is doing frequent syscalls for every chunk boundary. change in kernel made decode cheaper -> host now dominates.
claire: two orthogonal levers: 1) batching small gRPC writes into a short-window aggregator; 2) avoid utf8 work when payload already NFC normalized. Both low-risk.
maya: any downsides to holding frames longer? KV interactions?
devon: KV note: when we delay flush there's a chance multi-chunk requests serialize more at kv-shard leader during miss handling. For typical 1-3 chunk requests it's fine, but heavy multi-chunk tails can see +latency.
asher: I ran a microbench: enabling host mini-aggregator (max_bytes=3072, max_chunks=3, flush_timeout=6ms) reduced write syscall count by 4x, p95 down 28% for short streams. utf8 fast-path (is_normalized check) reduced normalize time median from 0.7ms -> 0.05ms.
claire: good. let's make mosaic of guards: aggregator default on; if chunk_count>12 OR request.body_size>64kb then bypass aggregator. Also gate utf8 by a cheap `bytes_equal(normalize(bytes), bytes)` check? we should choose a faster bloom-ish check.
asher: implemented `maybe_normalized` quick-check that inspects ascii-range + combining marks heuristic. Microbench shows false-negatives <0.5%.
maya: telemetry please: histograms for `host.parse.normalize_ms`, `host.streamer.grpc_writes`, `host.streamer.agg_bytes`, and a counter `host.streamer.agg_bypass_reason`.
devon: added metrics in branch:
```
metrics.hist("host.parse.normalize_ms", normalize_ms)
metrics.count("host.streamer.grpc_writes", grpc_write_calls)
metrics.histo("host.streamer.agg_bytes", agg_bytes)
metrics.tagged_count("host.streamer.agg_bypass_reason", reason)
```
ops-bot: deploy streamer-canary -> intake-2 (5%) by asher
ops-bot: rollout started: 5% -> 100% in 15m if healthy
claire: initial 15m snapshot: canary p95 -22% vs baseline on short streams. grpc_write_calls per request -3.9x. normalize_ms median 0.06ms.
maya: any impact on KV latency?
asher: saw a small bump (+4%) for a single heavy-customer who sends bursts of 30 chunks. Their requests hit the bypass rule? actually because our bypass was >12 chunks, the heavy customer still hit aggregation and saw +5% kv serialization.
devon: fix: add per-tenant override and a stricter bypass for kv_miss paths: if kv_miss && chunk_count>6 then bypass. That reduces heavy-user regression.
claire: roll updated canary to 20% with that rule. ops-bot?
ops-bot: deploy streamer-canary-v2 -> intake-2 (20%)
ops-bot: rollout complete: 20%
claire: new metrics: heavy-customer kv latencies back to baseline; overall p95 still -19%. CPU on proxy pods +5%.
maya: good trade. PR checklist: include microbench scripts, flame snapshots, config flags `host.streamer.agg_bytes`, `host.streamer.agg_chunks`, `host.streamer.agg_timeout_ms`, `host.preproc.utf8_quickcheck=true`, and per-tenant bypass toggle.
asher: also add a note in kernel-selection doc: short-seq kernels shift work to host, so must evaluate host batching as part of kernel rollout testing. I'll append a short matrix (seq_len vs host_work).
devon: agreed. schedule a 20m postmortem sync tomorrow to finalize thresholds and default config.
maya: thanks everyone. labels: perf, host-parse, grpc, kvcache. I'll file the PR and ping reviewers.
